sections.content:
You know *habrá* + past participle (*futuro perfecto*) for actions finished before a future deadline from B1 Unit 22, which mentioned its guessing use without practising it. In geopolitical analysis, both uses are central.

First, the **conjectural *futuro perfecto*** expresses a measured inference about a recent past cause whose effects are visible now: *el retraso en el puerto habrá encarecido el abastecimiento* ('the port delay has probably driven up supply costs'). Notice the contrast with simple-future conjecture, which guesses about the **present** (*el bloque buscará ahora un contrapeso*).

Second, when projecting long-term structural shifts by a future milestone (*para el final de la década*, *para entonces*), analysis frequently pairs the *futuro perfecto* with passive or reflexive *se*: *para entonces se habrán diversificado las rutas de abastecimiento*.

sections.title: Two C1 uses of *futuro perfecto*
rows: *los puertos ya habrán absorbido el retraso* ('have probably absorbed')
*el bloque negociará ahora nuevas rutas* ('is probably negotiating now')
*al cierre del decenio, la región habrá reconfigurado su logística*

items.spanish: El bloqueo temporal del estrecho habrá encarecido el transporte de mercancías.
items.english: The temporary blockage of the strait has probably made the transport of goods more expensive.

items.spanish: Los analistas ya habrán evaluado el impacto sobre las cadenas de abastecimiento.
items.english: Analysts have probably already assessed the impact on supply chains.

items.spanish: Para el final de la década se habrán diversificado los corredores marítimos.
items.english: By the end of the decade, maritime corridors will have been diversified.

items.spanish: Para entonces, las economías regionales habrán consolidado un contrapeso propio.
items.english: By then, the regional economies will have consolidated a counterweight of their own.

sections.content: Use *habrá / habrán* + past participle for conjecture about a **completed recent event** (*ya habrán firmado*), and the simple future for conjecture about what is happening **now** (*estarán negociando* / *buscarán*). The past participle stays invariable (*se habrán reconfigurado*, never *reconfiguradas*).
